participants.note: reported that thread start/exit logs spammed to the point rate-limiting engaged
tested and measured speedups on IBD and reindex-chainstate, suggested sliding window and index reusability, and ACKed

claims.harm: Thread start and exit logging spams debug logs until rate-limiting kicks in
claims.quote: Note that this spams ` blockread.* thread start/exit` debug logs to the point that rate-limiting kicks
claims.settled_by_quote: I’ve pushed a fix that keeps it alive on `Chainstate`

claims.harm: Prefetched blocks for an invalid branch stay in memory indefinitely
claims.quote: When a block was rejected, blocks read ahead for its branch could remain in memory indefinitely.

support.reason: Managed to see speedup in IBD benchmarks by having one local node bind to 10 ports and the other connect to all 10. I did this and reindex-chainstate with an i7 and i5 machine. Nice speedups, especially for reindex-chainstate.

result.notes: fanquake's thread log spam objection was resolved by preserving the thread pool across activations on Chainstate. w0xlt's concern that rejected blocks leave prefetched descendants in memory remains open.
